title: Levels of control and the seven tolerances
blurb: Explain how tolerances are delegated through the four management levels and define each of the seven tolerance areas.
question: Who sets work package tolerances, and which tolerances are NOT agreed in a work package description?

teach.body: Formally, a tolerance is the permissible deviation above and below a plan's target for time, cost, scope, quality, benefits, risk and sustainability before the matter must be escalated to the next management level. In plain English: each level is told 'this is the target, and this much either side is yours to manage'. Tolerances set the limits of delegated authority.

teach.h: Who sets what, and what comes back up
head: Level
Sets
Receives
teach.caption: The business layer sits outside the project management team but sets the project's overall tolerances.
Seven performance targets, seven tolerances. Sustainability is new in PRINCE2 7.

head: Tolerance
Permissible variation
rows: Under or over delivery of benefits
Later or earlier than the target date
Limits on the plan's aggregated risks

teach.h: Work package tolerances are narrower in range
teach.body: When the project manager authorizes a work package, its description sets tolerances for scope, cost and time. Benefits and quality tolerances are not agreed in a work package description: benefits belong to the business case level, and quality is controlled through the product descriptions and their quality specifications. The team manager works inside these limits and sets limits for team members.

At Ashby Vale Hospitals Trust, the trust's capital committee (business layer) gives the ward project a cost tolerance of plus or minus 8%. The project board, chaired by executive Dr Helen Okafor, gives project manager Tomasz Nowak a stage cost tolerance of plus or minus 5%. Tomasz then gives the electrical team manager, Grace Elliott, a work package with scope, cost and time tolerances. Each level manages freely inside its own limits.

teach.h: Target plus tolerance: a stage budget
teach.caption: Tolerance works both ways: a large underspend or early finish can also need escalating.

teach.text: Classic traps: (1) There are SEVEN tolerances, not six: sustainability is new. (2) Data and systems do not set tolerances; the management levels do. (3) The project board sets stage tolerances; the business layer sets project tolerances. (4) A work package description holds scope, cost and time tolerances, not benefits or quality tolerances.

items: A tolerance is a permissible deviation above and below a plan's target.
Four levels: business layer, project board, project manager, team manager.
Business layer: project tolerances. Board: stage tolerances. PM: work package tolerances.
Seven areas: benefits, cost, time, quality, scope, sustainability, risk.
Work package descriptions carry scope, cost and time tolerances.

summary: You can now explain how the business layer, project board and project manager delegate tolerances down the four management levels. You can define the seven tolerance areas and say which ones a work package description carries.

A.why: The business layer, outside the project management team, sets the overall project tolerances, often in the project mandate.

whyNot.0: The project board sets stage tolerances within the project tolerances.
whyNot.1: The executive works with the board on stage tolerances, not project tolerances.
whyNot.3: The project manager sets work package tolerances.

A.q: Which is one of the seven tolerance areas in PRINCE2 7?
A.why: The seven are benefits, cost, time, quality, scope, sustainability and risk.

whyNot.0: Resources are planned, but they are not a tolerance area.
whyNot.2: Stakeholders are engaged through the people element, not given a tolerance.
whyNot.3: Communication is managed through the communication management approach.

A.q: What does the scope tolerance limit?
options: Permissible variation of the plan's products
A.why: Scope tolerance is the permissible variation of the plan's products.

whyNot.1: Overspend against budget is limited by the cost tolerance.
whyNot.2: Variation from agreed quality criteria is limited by the quality tolerance.
whyNot.3: Limits on the plan's aggregated risks are the risk tolerance.

B.q: Which tolerances are set in a work package description?
B.why: A work package description sets permissible deviations for scope, cost and time; benefits and quality tolerances are not agreed in it.

whyNot.1: Benefits tolerances are not agreed in a work package description.
whyNot.2: Quality tolerances are not agreed in a work package description.
whyNot.3: Neither quality nor benefits tolerances are agreed in a work package description.

B.q:
Which two statements about tolerances are correct?
1. Tolerance can apply above and below a target.
2. Data and systems set the stage tolerances.
3. The project manager sets work package tolerances.
4. There are six tolerance areas.
B.why: Tolerance is a deviation above and below a target (1), and the project manager sets work package tolerances (3).

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is false: management levels set tolerances, not data and systems.
whyNot.1: Both are false: the board sets stage tolerances, and PRINCE2 7 has seven tolerance areas.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is false: sustainability makes seven.

B.q: What does the risk tolerance limit?
options: The number of risks in the register
The cost of the risk budget
B.why: Risk tolerance sets limits on the plan's aggregated risks.

whyNot.0: Tolerance is about aggregated exposure, not a count of entries.
whyNot.2: The risk budget funds responses; the tolerance limits aggregated risk.
whyNot.3: Assessment effort is not what the risk tolerance limits.

C.q: Which level sets stage tolerances, and which report does it receive on stage progress?
options: The business layer; the end project report
The project manager; the checkpoint report
The project board; the highlight report
The team manager; the exception report
C.why: The project board sets stage tolerances and receives highlight reports (and exception reports) from the project manager.

whyNot.0: The business layer sets project tolerances; the end project report is a closure report.
whyNot.1: The project manager sets work package tolerances and receives checkpoint reports.
whyNot.3: Team managers work within work package tolerances; exception reports go to the board.

C.q: A stage is forecast to finish well under budget, beyond its cost tolerance. Which statement is correct?
options: It is a deviation beyond tolerance that the board should know about
It needs no action because cost tolerance applies to overspends
It is a quality tolerance matter for the senior supplier
It is recorded as a lesson and handled at project closure
C.why: Cost tolerance covers overspend and underspend, so a forecast underspend beyond tolerance is also an exception for the board.

whyNot.1: Cost tolerance includes underspend as well as overspend.
whyNot.2: Budget variation is a cost tolerance matter, not quality.
whyNot.3: A forecast breach is escalated during the stage, not left until closure.

C.q: Who sets tolerances for team members, and within which limits?
options: The project manager, within stage tolerances
The project board, within project tolerances
The project support, within the stage plan
The team manager, within work package tolerances
C.why: The team manager sets tolerances and constraints for team members, inside the work package tolerances agreed with the project manager.

whyNot.0: The project manager sets work package tolerances for team managers, not tolerances for individual team members.
whyNot.1: The board sets stage tolerances for the project manager.
whyNot.2: Project support provides administration; it does not delegate tolerances.

reteach.title: Pocket money at three levels
reteach.question: How do nested allowances explain the four levels of tolerance?

blocks.body: A family gives a teenager £100 for a school trip, plus or minus £10. The teenager gives a friend £30 to buy the group's lunch, plus or minus £5. If lunch will cost £40, the friend tells the teenager. If the whole trip will cost £120, the teenager tells the family. Each level holds a smaller allowance inside the one above, just as project, stage and work package tolerances nest.

blocks.text: The friend buying lunch never had a 'benefits' allowance: work package tolerances cover scope, cost and time only.

explain.body: A tolerance is the permissible deviation above and below a plan's target before escalation to the next level.

options: A reserve set aside to fund approved changes
The business's attitude towards taking risk
A permissible deviation from a plan's target
The agreed target completion date for a stage
test.why: Tolerance is the permissible deviation above and below a plan's target before escalation.

whyNot.0: Money set aside for approved changes is the change budget.
whyNot.1: The business's attitude to risk is its risk appetite.
whyNot.3: The target date is the target itself; tolerance is the room around it.

explain.body: The project is managed by exception between four management levels: business layer, project board, project manager and team manager.

test.why: The project board sets stage tolerances for the project manager.

whyNot.0: The business layer sets project tolerances.
whyNot.1: The project manager sets work package tolerances.
whyNot.2: The team manager works within work package tolerances.

explain.body: Benefits, cost, time, quality, scope, sustainability and risk. Sustainability tolerance places limits on agreed sustainability metrics.

options: Variation from the agreed quality criteria
Variation from the planned completion date
test.why: Sustainability tolerance places limits on the agreed metrics for sustainability.

whyNot.0: Variation from quality criteria is the quality tolerance.
whyNot.2: Variation from forecast benefits is the benefits tolerance.
whyNot.3: Variation from the end date is the time tolerance.

explain.body: Work package descriptions set scope, cost and time tolerances. Benefits and quality tolerances are not agreed at this level.

test.q: Which tolerance is NOT agreed in a work package description?
test.why: Benefits (and quality) tolerances are not agreed in a work package description.

whyNot.1: Cost tolerance is set in the work package description.
whyNot.2: Time tolerance is set in the work package description.
whyNot.3: Scope tolerance is set in the work package description.
